explain.say: Pick up any packet of food and turn it over. There's a little table full of numbers. It looks tricky, but it's easy once you know the secret! The board shows a breakfast cereal label. Each bar tells you how many grams are in 100 grams of the food.

explain.say: Look at the biggest bar, carbohydrate, 70 grams. That's the main energy food in cereal, from grains. Now see the bar under it, of which sugars, 20 grams. So 20 of those 70 grams are sugar, about 5 teaspoons. Is that more or less than you guessed?

explain.say: See the tiny salt bar, 0.8 grams? Small numbers still matter. Some countries, like the UK, add traffic-light colours: green for low, amber for medium, red for high. Using the per 100 grams column lets you compare two foods fairly.

explain.say: Fantastic, you can read a label! Look at the colours for this cereal: fat and saturated fat are green, low, while sugars and salt are amber, medium. Challenge: next time you shop, compare two cereals per 100 grams and find the one with less sugar!

faq.q: What does per 100 g mean on a food label?
faq.a: It tells you how many grams of each nutrient are in 100 grams of the food. Because every packet uses the same 100 grams, you can compare foods fairly.
asks: Why do labels say per 100 g?

faq.q: What does of which sugars mean?
faq.a: It shows how much of the carbohydrate is sugar. So carbohydrate 70 grams, of which sugars 20 grams, means 20 of the 70 grams are sugar.
asks: How much sugar is in my cereal?

faq.q: What do the traffic light colours mean?
faq.a: Used in the UK and some other countries, green means low, amber medium and red high, for fat, saturated fat, sugars and salt per 100 grams.
asks: What does red on a food label mean?

faq.a: A unit for the energy in food. Labels show energy in kilojoules and kilocalories; one kilocalorie is about 4.2 kilojoules.

faq.q: Why is fibre on the label?
faq.a: Fibre comes from plants and helps your gut work well. Foods with more fibre, like whole grains, beans and vegetables, keep you full for longer.

facts: On UK front-of-pack labels, sugars count as high above 22.5 g per 100 g and low at 5 g or less.

quiz.show: A label says carbohydrate 70 g, of which sugars 20 g. How much is sugar?
quiz.why: Of which sugars means 20 of the 70 grams of carbohydrate are sugar.

wrong.1: 70 grams is all the carbohydrate, not just the sugar.
wrong.2: You don't add them; the sugar is part of the 70 grams.
